title: From Zero to Leaderboard: Agent Evaluation — Wolfram Ravenwolf, Weights & Biases
talk_summary: Wolfram Ravenwolf demonstrates building reproducible agent evals by treating benchmark, harness, sandbox, agent, model endpoint, and settings as one pinned configuration, running multiple trials, and inspecting traces. He argues single average scores hide reliability, token cost, refusals, and infra failures, so leaderboards should expose distributions and evidence.

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat model, agent harness, benchmark version, sandbox image, provider route, and sampling settings as one configuration; pin versions and record them so comparisons are reproducible.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you are actually benchmarking a specific configuration

takeaways.what_they_do: Run each eval multiple times and report average, consistency (tasks solved every run), ceiling (solved at least once), and worst/best spread instead of one average.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A single run is benchmark lottery.
takeaways.numbers: 5 runs; 89 tasks; 430+ runs; example 79% to 60% spread

takeaways.what_they_do: Measure tokens and dollar cost per run/task, because a nominally cheap model can burn more tokens and cost more than a stronger model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a cheaper and faster model takes longer and costs more than one of the bigger models because it just used so many tokens
takeaways.numbers: Gemini 3.5 Flash: 1.65B tokens/$620 vs GPT-5.5: 136M tokens/$497

takeaways.what_they_do: Use full agent trajectories as evidence behind scores; inspect refusals, overthinking, tool errors, and verifier failures rather than trusting aggregate bars.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The bar is a claim, the trace is evidence.
takeaways.numbers: Fable: 13 refusals, $11k eval cost; Opus max thinking lowered score

takeaways.what_they_do: Run each eval in a fresh sandbox and classify failures; retry sandbox/inference errors but count model-caused crashes as real failures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if I don't retry a task and it fails because a sandbox crashed, I get a bad score for the model. But it wasn't the model's fault.

takeaways.what_they_do: Provider context is often truncated below model max; higher thinking can cause overthinking and lower score under fixed timeout; tune per model/agent.
takeaways.numbers: GLM 5.2 served at 256K not 1M; Opus max thinking decreased score
